title: Can one score cutoff judge every decode?
question: Under the original source beam and English model, how do planted recovery, text register and length/beam setting affect the interpretation of a fixed −5.5 cutoff?
reader_question: Could a good-looking score hide an incorrect decode?
summary: Four of 28 synthetic decodes pass the English-score cutoff while recovering less than 90% of the planted text. Five source text registers and three fresh conditional-null settings show why the same cutoff needs matched controls.
finding: In 28 source-derived L7 mechanism plants at 240 runes, four runs clear −5.5 while recovering less than 90% of the planted runes. Seven baseline plants recover exactly; paired rejection has 25.8% median recovery, one free advance 95%, and free advances at q=.02 give 72.1%. Fifteen correct/wrong-key register pairs reproduce the corresponding saved source subset. Fresh 120-draw nulls at L31/bw120, L120/bw400 and L400/bw120 give tail-excess scales 0.35236, 0.13471 and 0.06090; each uses only 11 upper-tail exceedances.
reader_finding: Four synthetic decodes passed the score cutoff while recovering less than 90% of the known text. The score ranges also changed across text registers and decoder settings, so a score alone cannot certify a correct reading.
limitations: Finite source-derived controls, not an LP2 key search. Missing original modern-English/Mabinogion and Welsh inputs and derived vowel-deletion panels are excluded. Five available registers include two English texts, not five languages. Null settings change both length and beam width and have only 120 draws each; the eleven-point tail estimates do not calibrate a large-search error rate. The archived fixtures support exact finite replay, not full corpus reconstruction; the packaged plan was written after execution.
reader_limit: These controls do not identify LP2’s language or cipher. The null samples are too small to validate a cutoff for a large key search.
next_steps: For a proposed solving tool, predeclare its complete search rule and verify recovery of held-out planted texts plus a matched search-maximum null before interpreting a high score.

scope.representation: Fixed source-derived GP29 plaintext/ciphertext/key fixtures, English quadgram counts and a source ciphertext prefix used only for order-destroying conditional controls.
scope.procedure: Replay the unchanged source beam on fifteen paired register plants and twenty-eight mechanism plants; generate 120 fixed-seed shuffled-prefix nulls per setting; independently recalculate rune recovery, quadgram scores and null summaries.
scope.parameters: Five registers × three L120 trials with correct and wrong keys; four mechanisms × seven L240 plants; source beam width 400/max_skip 3; score cutoff −5.5 and recovery reference 90%; three null settings L31/bw120,L120/bw400,L400/bw120 × 120 draws.
scope.exclusions: Full 67-case L7 envelope; original missing EN_MODERN/CY and derived vowel panels; six-model archive rescoring; G3 difference-floor census; independently preregistered corpus selection; large-search tail calibration; real LP2 keys or cipher exclusions.

review.reviewer: Exact-source finite replay plus independent stored-trace score/recovery/null arithmetic checks

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library only. No network, external corpus, GnuPG, NumPy or AI calls are needed for the packaged replay.

sources.label: Pinned original L7 instrument and controls

visuals.caption: Median planted rune recovery for four original L7 mechanisms. Four of twenty-eight decodes clear the score cutoff but recover less than 90% of the text.
Five text registers use the same marks and axis; each has three correct-key plants. The dashed line is the source −5.5 cutoff.
Observed ranges and means of 120 shuffled controls at each length/beam setting. These small samples do not calibrate large-search tail probabilities.
